title: Search for free non-Abelian anyons in paired composite-fermion states
abstract: The even-denominator fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, understood as topological superconductors of composite fermions, are predicted to support elementary quasiparticles (QPs) or quasiholes (QHs) obeying non-Abelian braid statistics. Using the microscopic framework of parton theory, we investigate many experimentally observed paired composite-fermion states and find that their elementary QPs and QHs in general bind to form Abelian molecules, thus obscuring non-Abelian braid statistics. An exception is the $ν=1/2$ state in wide quantum wells, where our calculations show free QPs or QHs; we thus identify this state as an especially promising candidate for realizing and studying non-Abelian braid statistics. We also indicate how the study of such bound states can help reveal the topological structure of the state.
summary: This theoretical study investigates the stability of quasiparticles in even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states to determine if they exhibit non-Abelian statistics. Using parton theory and numerical simulations, the authors find that binding generally obscures the desired statistics, except for the $\nu=1/2$ state in wide quantum wells, which is proposed as a key platform for realizing non-Abelian anyons.
main_problem: The study investigates whether the quasiparticles (QPs) or quasiholes (QHs) in even-denominator fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states bind together, which determines if the state supports non-Abelian braid statistics.
main_result: Generally, QPs/QHs bind into Abelian molecules, obscuring non-Abelian statistics, with the $\nu=1/2$ state in wide quantum wells being identified as a promising exception where free non-Abelian statistics might exist.
method: The authors use the microscopic framework of parton theory, employing the Metropolis-Gibbs-Hastings algorithm to calculate the binding energy of two-particle excitations (QPs/QHs) in the Lowest Landau Level (LLL).
model_or_system: The system is based on even-denominator FQH states, modeled using composite fermions (CFs) and analyzed on the Haldane spherical geometry. The calculations examine various parton representations ($\bar{2}213$, etc.) across different material platforms like wide quantum wells and graphene.
key_observables: Binding energy ($\Delta^2$), relative angular momentum ($L_{\text{rel}}$), and the existence of free QPs/QHs.
important_parameters: Filling factors ($\nu=5/2, 1/2, 1/4$), relative angular momentum channels (odd/even parity), and the ratio of well width to magnetic length ($w/\ell_B$).
main_assumptions: The analysis neglects Landau Level (LL) mixing and transverse subband mixing when projecting the physics onto the ideal 2D LLL.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the binding energy ($\Delta_2$) of two QHs and two QPs across different parton phases and LLs, showing the dependence on $L_{\text{rel}}$ and the relative stability of the bound states.
paper_structure: The paper systematically constructs the wavefunctions for two-particle excitations in various CF states, calculates the binding energy using numerical methods, and compares the results across different physical regimes (e.g., different LLs or quantum well widths) to pinpoint the conditions for non-Abelian behavior.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the topological nature of fractional quantum Hall states, which is a cornerstone of strongly correlated electron physics. The search for robust non-Abelian excitations is highly relevant to understanding topological quantum computation.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Panel (a) schematically depicts the parton ground state Ψ¯2¯2111; the arrow on top shows the magnetic field direction. Panels (b) and (d) show two quasiholes (QHs) and two quasiparticles (QPs) (marked by yellow boxes) in the odd-parity channel, and panels (c) and (e) in the even-parity channel. Note that a QP of the parton with filling factor 2 produces, due to complex conjugation, a QH of the ν = 1/2 state.

FIG. 2: Binding energy ∆2 of two quasiholes (dashed) and two quasiparticles (solid) for ¯2213 at ν = 1/2 (top), and 2213 and ¯2215 at ν = 1/4 (middle and bottom), as a function of w/ℓB, for N ∼100 electrons. The width and density dependence approximately collapses onto w/ℓB (Fig. S2). Blue (red) curves show even (odd) channels; L⋆ rel is indicated. Gray bands mark the experimental onset of the fractional quantum Hall effect, obtained from Figs. 3 and 12 of Ref. [19]: w/ℓB = 8.9(2) at ν = 1/2 [17, 20, 60] and w/ℓB ≈12.4–12.8 at ν = 1/4 [18, 33]. Our results are meaningful only to the right of the vertical bands.
